rationale: As a 20-option portfolio, this sheet only shows 8 visible families and one family dominates by roughly half of the set. Most candidates are incremental edits of the same long-bar hall: repeated slab/prismatic chassis, repeated frontage-notch access moves, and repeated roof profiles. The portfolio does contain a few useful alternatives, especially the block/open-court versions and the oblique/cantilevered mass, but overall the set lacks the minimum diversity and program-specific section language required for a passing gymnasium portfolio. The next revision needs more materially different long-span hall families, not more roof tweaks.

required_next_relations: Generate at least 12 additional masses that are not minor roof edits of a slab/bar chassis; introduce new spatial families through profiled hall, carve-void, lift, bridge, terrace, and cut-corner moves.

Keep the dominant hall legible, but vary section logic: high monitor, asymmetric sawtooth, shallow dome/curved span, split-roof hall, and displaced service spine are all valid if the hall remains primary.
Ensure at least one family clearly expresses west-side access as a threshold carve or lifted entry, not only as a notch in the bar.
Avoid repeating the same long rectangular footprint; use different plan depths, offsets, and section heights so the portfolio reads as 10+ materially distinct massing families.
Do not use abstract box-only or pyramid-like roofing; every option must read as a gymnasium hall with span, daylight, and subordinate support volume.
